_comment: Every command is wrapped in the bootstrap guard: a fresh plugin-cache version ships from git WITHOUT binaries (they arrive via doctor --fix), and an unguarded hook crash-storms every tool call in that window (measured, 0.7.0 dance). The guard degrades to ONE stderr line pointing at the fix. Guard shell is Git Bash on every platform (verified live: the 0.7.0 failures came from /usr/bin/bash).

PreToolUse._comment: ONE hook for this event (#201 step 3). The secrets gate and the push-freeze guard are still separate UNITS with OPPOSITE postures — the gate fails CLOSED and can deny, including on an undecodable payload (#211); the freeze guard NEVER blocks, because the freeze is a commitment the human may consciously override. The merge keeps both: deny wins and only one permission document is emitted, while warnings survive a denial because the operator needs both facts. The matcher is the UNION of the units' own (the gate watches WebFetch|WebSearch|Bash, the guard only Bash), and each unit still checks its own applicability so merging cannot widen what it acts on.

hooks.command: B="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/sc-pretooluse"; if [ -x "$B" ] || [ -x "$B.exe" ]; then exec "$B"; fi; echo 'prosthetic-conscience: hook binaries missing (new plugin version?) — run /prosthetic-conscience:doctor --fix' >&2

PostToolUse._comment: ONE hook for this event (#201 step 3). The quality gate and the recall index are still separate UNITS with their own packages and tests; they now run in one process over one shared context. Measured (hook-surface-spike.md §4b): the client runs an event's hooks in PARALLEL, so this merge runs its units concurrently simply to MATCH that — parity is the floor. What it buys is what two processes could not share: the payload parsed once, the project root resolved once, ONE writer for the hook log (those two appends were concurrent by design), and a place for expensive reads to be memoised as they arrive. The matcher is the UNION of the units' own, and each unit still checks its own applicability.

hooks.command: B="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/sc-posttooluse"; if [ -x "$B" ] || [ -x "$B.exe" ]; then exec "$B"; fi; echo 'prosthetic-conscience: hook binaries missing (new plugin version?) — run /prosthetic-conscience:doctor --fix' >&2

B="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/sc-toolchain-nudge"; if [ -x "$B" ] || [ -x "$B.exe" ]; then exec "$B"; fi; echo 'prosthetic-conscience: hook binaries missing (new plugin version?) — run /prosthetic-conscience:doctor --fix' >&2

hooks._comment: No matcher: restore fires on EVERY source, compact included. SessionStart is the only hook that can inject at a compaction boundary — PostCompact cannot, and runs after this anyway (plans/hook-surface-spike.md §3a). A source filter here silently removes continuity from the boundary the design exists for.
hooks.command: B="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/sc-checkpoint-restore"; if [ -x "$B" ] || [ -x "$B.exe" ]; then exec "$B"; fi; echo 'prosthetic-conscience: hook binaries missing (new plugin version?) — run /prosthetic-conscience:doctor --fix' >&2

B="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/sc-postcompact-observe"; if [ -x "$B" ] || [ -x "$B.exe" ]; then exec "$B"; fi; echo 'prosthetic-conscience: hook binaries missing (new plugin version?) — run /prosthetic-conscience:doctor --fix' >&2

FileChanged._comment: No matcher: watchPaths is registered dynamically by sc-checkpoint-restore from the note's own trigger surfaces, so the set is per-session and cannot be written here. The hook narrows what the watch cannot — watchPaths takes directories, never patterns (hook-surface-spike.md §6) — by matching file_path back to the check that claimed the surface. Changes under .claude/ are ignored so the hooks' own writes cannot re-trigger them.

hooks.command: B="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/sc-filechanged-rearm"; if [ -x "$B" ] || [ -x "$B.exe" ]; then exec "$B"; fi; echo 'prosthetic-conscience: hook binaries missing (new plugin version?) — run /prosthetic-conscience:doctor --fix' >&2

PreCompact._comment: -event is passed explicitly rather than read from the payload: the Phase 0 spike never verified that hook input carries hook_event_name, and this plan already spent a cycle on a capability inferred from an input field. PreCompact is the ONLY event where this binary speaks — its stdout becomes the summarizer's custom instructions.

hooks.command: B="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/sc-checkpoint-seal"; if [ -x "$B" ] || [ -x "$B.exe" ]; then exec "$B" -event PreCompact; fi; echo 'prosthetic-conscience: hook binaries missing (new plugin version?) — run /prosthetic-conscience:doctor --fix' >&2

SessionEnd._comment: No matcher: SessionEnd.reason is 'other' for a headless `claude -p` run, not one of clear/logout/prompt_input_exit (measured, hook-surface-spike.md §4). Matching only the interactive reasons would skip exactly the sessions with no human watching. A session that ends without ever compacting otherwise leaves nothing.

hooks.command: B="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/sc-checkpoint-seal"; if [ -x "$B" ] || [ -x "$B.exe" ]; then exec "$B" -event SessionEnd; fi; echo 'prosthetic-conscience: hook binaries missing (new plugin version?) — run /prosthetic-conscience:doctor --fix' >&2

SubagentStop._comment: Shares this event with gray-area's capture hook by design — Claude Code merges hook configurations across plugins, and each writes its own file (context-checkpointing.md §9). This one seals the note keyed by agent_id, because every subagent shares the parent's session_id.

hooks.command: B="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/sc-checkpoint-seal"; if [ -x "$B" ] || [ -x "$B.exe" ]; then exec "$B" -event SubagentStop; fi; echo 'prosthetic-conscience: hook binaries missing (new plugin version?) — run /prosthetic-conscience:doctor --fix' >&2

PostToolUseFailure._comment: No matcher: a spin is a spin whatever tool it runs through, and anti-spinning names none. The counter keys on (tool, target) itself, and skips is_interrupt so the rule's other half — honor the cancel — does not fight this one (measured: plans/hook-surface-spike.md §2).

hooks.command: B="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/sc-strike-counter"; if [ -x "$B" ] || [ -x "$B.exe" ]; then exec "$B"; fi; echo 'prosthetic-conscience: hook binaries missing (new plugin version?) — run /prosthetic-conscience:doctor --fix' >&2
